'''Barak Kol''' ({{Langx|he|ברק קול}}; born August 1968) is an [[Israeli citizenship law|Israeli]] [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who studies fundamental laws, high-energy physics, and [[general relativity]]. He holds the Michael Polak chair in theoretical physics at [[the Racah Institute of Physics]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

== Biography ==
Kol completed his BSc in physics and mathematics at Tel Aviv University in 1989, following which he did his military service in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]]. Afterwards, he completed his PhD at Stanford University in 1998 under the guidance of [[Leonard Susskind]], during which he coined the term "(p,q) webs." His most widely cited paper is on the subject and has over 500 citations.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Barak Kol |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=gduavmgAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-06-08 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

Following the completion of his PhD, Kol was a postdoctoral fellow at Tel Aviv University (1998-2000) and at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (2000-2002). During the latter, he was hosted by [[Nathan Seiberg]]. Afterwards, he became a faculty member at the Racah Institute of Physics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Racah Institute of Physics |url=http://old.phys.huji.ac.il/~barak_kol/ |access-date=2022-06-08 |website=old.phys.huji.ac.il}}</ref>

Kol's previous research topics include phase transitions in [[Black brane|black strings]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kol |first=Barak |date=2006-01-01 |title=The phase transition between caged black holes and black strings |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370157305004126 |journal=Physics Reports |language=en |volume=422 |issue=4 |pages=119–165 |doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2005.10.001 |issn=0370-1573|arxiv=hep-th/0411240 |bibcode=2006PhR...422..119K |s2cid=8270306 }}</ref> [[Effective field theory|effective field theories]] in general relativity,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kol |first1=Barak |last2=Smolkin |first2=Michael |date=2008-06-24 |title=Non-relativistic gravitation: from Newton to Einstein and back |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/25/14/145011 |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |language=en |volume=25 |issue=14 |article-number=145011 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/25/14/145011 |issn=0264-9381|arxiv=0712.4116 |bibcode=2008CQGra..25n5011K |s2cid=119216835 }}</ref> [[black hole]]s in string theory,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kallosh |first1=Renata |last2=Kol |first2=Barak |date=1996-05-15 |title=E(7) symmetric area of the black hole horizon |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.53.R5344 |journal=Physical Review D |volume=53 |issue=10 |pages=R5344–R5348 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.53.R5344|pmid=10019889 |arxiv=hep-th/9602014 |bibcode=1996PhRvD..53.5344K |s2cid=2538247 }}</ref> and the [[three-body problem]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kol |first=Barak |date=2021-04-01 |title=Flux-based statistical prediction of three-body outcomes |journal=Celestial Mechanics and Dynamical Astronomy |language=en |volume=133 |issue=4 |article-number=17 |doi=10.1007/s10569-021-10015-x |issn=1572-9478|arxiv=2002.11496 |bibcode=2021CeMDA.133...17K |s2cid=219708954 }}</ref>

He was previously Head of the Physics Studies at the Racah Institute.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=מקור היסודות הכבדים גלי כבידה כוכבי ניוטרון |url=https://he-il.facebook.com/DeanStudTechnion/posts/1998374293759578/}}</ref>
